newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FORMER MP LAWS SAYS NZ FIRST PARTY FINISHED.
newsitem.headline: FORMER MP LAWS SAYS NZ FIRST PARTY FINISHED.

text.p: Former New Zealand First MP Michael Laws on Tuesday said the coalition had become more important to Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters than his party, and predicted NZ First would be finished at the next election.

"Winston Peters had ... decided something else in his mind.... The coalition was more important than NZ First. He was quite prepared to sacrifice the latter to preserve the former," Laws, once a close friend and advisor to Peters, said in his regular newspaper column.
"Which is why, after the next general election, there won't be a NZ First party. And unless a deal is struck (with National) in (Peters' seat of) Tauranga there won't even be a Winston," Laws said.
NZ First and the larger conservative National Party signed a coalition deal in December.
Laws was an advisor to Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton who was sacked last week. Earlier, he had been a researcher for Peters before becoming a National MP and then switching to NZ First.
He resigned his seat in 1996 after a minor scandal involving a signature on a local body poll.

Laws said at the election due in 1999 NZ First would not get anywhere near the five percent threshold which assures parties of their share of seats under New Zealand's German-style mixed member proportional electoral system.
NZ First won 13 percent of the vote at the October 1996 general election but its support has dropped to less than five percent in recent polls.
Earlier in the day, Peters confirmed that Laws had lost his job as advisor to Kirton. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
